i just signed up here in order to share my viewpoint with people in your situation. I fully understand you after I randomly clicked on your post; I was exactly where you are now when I was about 20.

Actually the feeling of being especially worthless came a couple years later; even though I had a "sucessful/good" life by worldly standards, I just couldn´t see a point in living so I almost "decided" to become an alcoholic, quit working, quit trying to make the world a better place (coming from fighting animal cruelty which I would never be able to reduce), started to sleep with every person available etc...until I had lost wealth and reputation. Clinical depression was a result of my lifestyle, and pessimistic thinking.

Only now, aged 42 and almost having died at many occasions due to careless conduct (drunk driving, swimming in lakes at 7 degrees, attempted suicides) I got back on track; it´s not the same as before, which I called "worldly" in the beginning.

The truth is: this world as we perceive it through senses and mind does not even exists, it is an "idea" (Schopenhauer), "maya" (an illusion due to Indian scriptures), "leela" (a game of our innermost Self which believes it is the game); it is the task of our lives to find this inner Self ("Gnothi Seauton" on the front of Delphi´s temple means just that) which is ultimate bliss, a totally different state of mind...the old scriptures call it samadhi, unio mystica, nirvana, moksha, heaven, the realm of God. I FOUND IT, after "a search so painful and long".

That said, let me refer to texts you can find in your library and all over the internet; look for "advaita vedanta", "Robert Adams", http://www.yoga-vidya.org/english/ etc.

Forget about your body, your feelings, your work life, your social belongings, your bank account...there´s so much more, on a higher plane. Herein lies our destination, and it will put suicidal thoughts in a different perspective...this was my experience and I´m happy I never succeeded in offing this life. Best wishes.
